newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
RESERVE BANK, MINISTRY FOR SOLUTION TO CRB ISSUE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Finance Ministry are looking for another finance company to take over CRB Caps as a whole or provide some other solution. As the ripples of the CRB Capital Markets (CRB Caps) case grow wider, both the RBI and the ministry are said to be working towards a solution that will be pragmatic and save it from actual liquidation. The Finance Ministry has asked the RBI to explore the possibilities of such a solution. Senior RBI officials met the chiefs of leading finance companies to discuss possibilities.
Financial Express
NINE EC NATIONS VOTE AGAINST INDIA

Nine European Union (EU) member nations have voted in favour of provisional anti-dumping duty on Indian bed-linen exports. The European Commission's (ECs) anti-dumping cell will formally disclose the extent of duty on each individual company by May 31. The penalised Indian companies have to present their defense within the next two weeks. Domestic textile industry sources have alleged that the majority vote in favour of imposition of duty is primarily to appease France which was the prime mover behind a similar duty on unbleached cotton fabrics from India earlier this month.
50 FIIS BEGIN EXERCISE TO GET RID OF FAKE SHARES

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have expressed deep concern over the growing cases of fake and forged shares that are entering the Indian capital markets. Frustrated by this, about 50 FIIs began a due diligence exercise to dematerialise their holdings. About 35 to 50 FIIs who had discussions with the senior officials of the national bourse and the national securities depository at a recent seminar in Hong Kong, are frustrated with the poor infrastructure available in dealing in physical papers. They told the national bourse and the Delhi bourse the growing number of fake and forged shares that are entering the system has only made matters worse.
OVER 400 FIRMS DECAMP WITH 5BLN

Over 400 companies listed on the Delhi bourse (DSE) have either quietly shifted offices or packed their bags without informing the exchange. DSE has now initiated an exercise to trace the companies which are estimated to be sitting pretty on five billion rupees raised through public issues. The exchange is banking on the Registrars of Companies of various regions in which the companies have their registered offices to track them down. The DSE management was surprised to learn that a number of companies were untraceable when it recently despatched bills for the listing fee to these companies through a courier agency.
Business Standard
FISCAL SOPS RECAST SOUGHT TO BOOST SAVINGS

The expert group on savings constituted by the government has recommended a complete overhaul of the existing pattern of fiscal incentives. The group has suggested that the present system of directing investments into various instruments like provident funds should be discarded. Instead, the government should fix a ceiling on the quantum of savings eligible for tax concessions, leaving the investor free to decide which instrument he wants to use. The decision to institute the committee was motivated by the government's concern that the savings rate has stagnated at the current level of about 24 percent.
NYSE TEAM ARRIVES TO WOO INDIAN CORPORATES

A New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) team is in India as part of efforts to invite listing by Indian companies. Sources said the chairman and CEO of the exchange would visit the country later this year. So far Indian companies have preferred European markets by making offerings of global depository receipts. Corporate sources said this is so as these bourses are less exacting about the disclosure and accounting norms. At present, several Indian companies are positioning themselves for floating ADRs in the US market and may well seek listing on the NYSE.
The Asian Age
APEX BANK INFUSING LIQUIDITY PRIOR TO AUCTION

The Reserve Bank of India has been mopping up dollars over the past one month ahead of auctions of government papers and treasury bills in the money market. This trend has been observed by foreign and money market dealers over the past month following the firming up of calls rates from around one percent in April to 5-10 percent during May. By infusing liquidity into the system, sources said the government could borrow at lower rates of interest.
The Observer
INDIAN PETROCHEMICALS' NET DIPS

Indian Petrochemicals Corporation (IPCL) has announced a 15 percent fall in net profit, leading to an immediate fall of its scrip price from 127.75 rupees to 124.25 rupees on the Bombay bourse. IPCL also announced significant falls in its gross profit, net sales and earnings per share. The major reason for this poor performance has been lower import tariffs and depressed international prices for chemicals and petrochemicals. This has affected the overall sales of the company. Moreover, the hike in fuel and raw material prices also led to a substantial increase in the expenses of the company.
RESERVE BANK SETTING UP INTER-AGENCY CELL

The Reserve Bank of India is setting up a coordination cell aimed at bridging the information gap between different government departments. These departments include the bourse regulator, department of company affairs, income tax and the credit rating agencies. The primary task of this agency will be to feed all the related agencies with information in order to prevent a repeat of the CRB Capitals case in which all the government departments were found to be lacking in vital information.
NORMS EASED FOR ELECTRONIC UNITS

Applications for electronic units in the electronics hardware technology parks (EHTP) and software technology parks (STP) will now get automatic approval. The industry ministry also assigned powers to grant post approval amendments, to the directors and designated officers of the STPs. The EHTP and STP schemes are for manufacturing electronic hardware and developing computer software for 100 percent exports. The ministry said that under the new procedures, applications fulfilling the conditions shall be approved within 15 days. The automatic approvals will be given if the project is not included in Schedule I or II of Notification No 477(E) of July 25, 1991.
